title: Dynamical resonances in PHANGS galaxies
question: Locate the bar corotation resonance (and derive ILR/OLR) in 46 barred PHANGS-ALMA galaxies with the gravitational torque method, and compare with literature CR estimates

what.value: Galaxy centers, orientations and distances from the PHANGS sample table v1.6

evidence.quote: The corresponding galaxy parameters such as distances, centers, and orientations are adopted from PHANGS sample table version v1.6

what.value: Inclination and position angle from CO kinematic analysis

evidence.quote: The inclination ($i$) and position angle (PA) are obtained from the CO kinematic analysis in (cite: Lang+20)

what.value: CO-based rotation curves used as proxy for circular velocity

evidence.quote: We use rotation curves based on CO kinematics from (cite: Lang+20) as a proxy for the circular velocity.
where $R_{\rm bar}$ is obtained from (cite: Querejeta+21)

what.value: Disk scale-lengths H_disk from NIR photometric decompositions

evidence.quote: where $H_{\rm disk}$ is obtained from photometric decompositions of NIR images ((cite: 2015ApJS..219....4S; Querejeta+21))

what.value: Stellar mass maps (S4G, ICA-corrected where recommended)

evidence.quote: Most stellar mass maps are obtained from the S$^4$G survey ((cite: Sheth+2010; Querejeta+15)).
This bar classification is based on infrared data from (cite: Buta+15).

what.value: Literature CR measurements (ten methods, 33 papers) used for comparison

evidence.quote: After this extensive literature research (ten different methods, 33 different papers)

what.value: Central ring radii from earlier work, used to test rings against the derived ILR

evidence.quote: Columns (4) and (5) contain the central ring positions registered in (cite: Querejeta+21) and (cite: Comeron+14) respectively.

recipe.goal: assemble gas and stellar mass maps
recipe.method: Use PHANGS-ALMA v4.0 strict-mask CO(2-1) moment-0 maps as the gas distribution and S4G/Spitzer 3.6 micron maps (ICA1, ICA2 or IRAC) as stellar mass maps
assumptions: Milky Way-like alpha_CO = 4.3 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1

recipe.method: Deproject gas and stellar maps with PA and inclination from Table 1
key_parameters: PA and i from CO kinematics (Lang+20)
assumptions: central structures are as flattened as the disk (no spherical bulge)

recipe.method: Convolve the stellar surface density with the kernel of a constant scale-height isothermal (sech^2) disk using Fourier transforms
assumptions: vertical distribution of an isothermal disk

recipe.method: Forces from the potential gradient; torque per unit mass t = xFy - yFx; multiplied by molecular gas to get angular momentum change

recipe.goal: azimuthally average torques and identify CR
recipe.method: Gas-weighted azimuthal average tau(R); CR taken as the negative-to-positive crossing with the largest amplitude within 0.75-2.25 R_bar
assumptions: steady state, gas distribution traces where gas spends its time

recipe.goal: derive pattern speed and Lindblad resonances
recipe.method: Omega_p from the angular velocity curve at R_CR; ILR/OLR from intersections of Omega -/+ kappa/2 with Omega_p using CO rotation curves
key_parameters: rotation curves in 150 pc wide radial bins
assumptions: epicyclic theory (valid only for small perturbations); observed rotation curve used as circular velocity

recipe.method: Perturb i, PA and center with Gaussian errors N=100 times, take 16th-84th percentile as error, add in quadrature; assign QF from max error relative to R_bar; also vary stellar mass map
key_parameters: QF=2 for 30% R_bar < err < 80% R_bar (QF=1 below, QF=3 above)

recipe.method: Spearman correlation and ratio of CR to literature CR, overall and per method, for QF=1,2 galaxies
Compute R = R_CR/R_bar and classify ultra-fast (<1), fast (1-1.4), slow (>1.4)

evidence.quote: the change from negative to positive torques at $R_{\rm CR}=6.4 \ \rm kpc$, is identified as the CR
we measure a pattern speed value of $\Omega_{\rm p} = 38.5\pm 4.7 \ \rm km \ s^{-1}\ kpc^{-1}$
This leads to an oILR at $R = 1.0\ \rm kpc$ and an OLR at $R = 9.6\ \rm kpc$.
we consider the CR to be at $R_{\rm CR}=5.2 \ \rm kpc$
we measure a pattern speed value of $\Omega_{\rm p} = 38.8\pm 1.8 \ \rm km \ s^{-1} \ kpc ^{-1}$
the selected crossing ($R_{\rm CR}=3.7 \ \rm kpc$) clearly represents the CR of the bar
we measure a pattern speed of $\Omega_{\rm p} = 44.2\pm4.5 \ \rm km \ s^{-1} \ kpc^{-1}$
torques robustly point to a CR at $R_{\rm CR} = 3.3 \ \rm kpc$
We measure a pattern speed $\Omega_{\rm p} = 68.2\pm3.5 \ \rm km \ s^{-1} \ kpc^{-1}$
We derived the $R_{\rm CR}$ for 38 out of 46 galaxies
we find that $20$ out of $46$ barred galaxies are reliable
$QF=1$ (8 galaxies, $\sim17\%$) or $QF=2$ (12 galaxies, $\sim26\%$)
we have a total of 19 ILRs (i.e., a $41\%$ of the sample)
Our average value, if we exclude those galaxies with $QF=3$, is $\mathcal{R}\sim 1.12 \pm 0.39$
we find six galaxies (30%) presenting fast bars, four galaxies (20%) presenting slow bars and ten galaxies (50%) presenting ultra-fast bars
